title: Comparing a timezone-aware datetime to a naive one doesn't give the wrong answer -- it refuses to answer at all
assumption: Two datetime objects can always be compared with < or == as long as they represent real moments in time.

input.description: Mixing a datetime parsed from a source that attaches a timezone (e.g. an API response with an offset) with one created locally via datetime.now() or a form field with no timezone info, then comparing or sorting them together.

what_goes_wrong: Sorting or comparing a list of datetimes where some came from a timezone-aware source and others didn't raises `TypeError` at the comparison, not at creation, often deep inside a sort() call far from where the mismatched datetime was built.
why: Python deliberately refuses to compare a 'naive' datetime (no attached tzinfo, interpretation of its clock reading is unstated) with an 'aware' one (tzinfo attached, unambiguous UTC instant) via the ordering operators (<, <=, >, >=), because there is no safe default assumption to make about what timezone the naive one is in. This is a documented decision, not a bug: Python could guess the naive value is UTC or local time, but either guess could silently be wrong, so it raises instead. Equality is the exception: since Python 3.3, == between a naive and an aware datetime returns False instead of raising, so a mixed pair silently never matches (the repro's last line).

repros.code:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

naive = datetime(2024, 1, 1)
aware = datetime(2024, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
try:
    naive < aware
except TypeError as e:
    print("TypeError:", e)

# Equality does NOT raise -- it just always says they're different, which is its own trap.
print("naive == aware (no error, but is this right?):", naive == aware)
repros.expected_output:
TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
naive == aware (no error, but is this right?): False
a < b: false | a.getTime() === b.getTime(): true

fix: Pick one representation (aware, ideally UTC) at every boundary where a datetime enters your system, and convert immediately; never let a naive and an aware datetime coexist in the same comparison, sort, or collection.
